rubric.criterion: Thesis: a defensible claim that establishes a line of reasoning (1 point).
rubric.example: Federal systems are more effective because they give distinct groups self-government, reducing pressure on the central state.

rubric.criterion: Evidence: two pieces of specific, relevant evidence from course countries (up to 2 points).
rubric.example: Nigeria uses federalism and the federal character principle to share power among its many ethnic groups. The UK, though unitary, used devolution to Scotland and Wales to accommodate national identities, showing the value of shared power. China's unitary approach in Xinjiang relies on coercion rather than accommodation.

rubric.criterion: Reasoning: explains why the evidence supports the claim (1 point).
rubric.example: Connects each example back to the thesis rather than just describing it.

rubric.criterion: Alternative perspective: responds with refutation, concession or rebuttal (1 point).
rubric.example: Critics argue federalism can entrench divisions and fuel separatism; but without it, groups may turn to more radical demands.
